answer: Mutual underwriting pools: every agent joins a pool of twelve whose bonds insure each other's honesty. One caught fake makes the whole pool pay, and its premiums rise, so pools audit every applicant and expel bad apples together. A farm must either pass twelve strangers' screening per identity or form its own pool, where its clones' failures echo as correlated claims and the premium explodes. Like an orchard sharing one irrigation prism, one poisoned root raises the water price for every tree; the cost lands per identity, and bulk buying only buys a bigger bill.
